programs.name: smooth2
programs.purpose: Smooth a uniformly sampled two-dimensional float array, optionally within a window.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SMOOTH2 --- SMOOTH a uniformly sampled 2d array of data, within a user-

params.name: n1
params.description: Number of samples in the fast dimension.

params.name: n2
params.description: Number of samples in the slow dimension.

params.name: r1
params.description: Smoothing parameter in the first dimension; internally scaled to r1*r1*0.25.

params.name: r2
params.description: Smoothing parameter in the second dimension; internally scaled to r2*r2*0.25.

params.name: win
params.description: Four window bounds: first-dimension start and exclusive end, then second-dimension start and exclusive end.

params.name: rw
params.description: Window-edge smoothing parameter; internally scaled to rw*rw*0.25.

params.name: efile
params.description: Optional file for n1 binary floats containing cumulative relative RMS error by first-dimension index.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Sequential tridiagonal solves use float arithmetic and depend on operation order; double constants and sqrt introduce float/double mixing. Error-file sums accumulate across both dimensions without resetting at each depth. The first-dimension solve updates f[0] before assigning f[n1-2], which overwrites that update when n1=2; small or invalid dimensions and out-of-range or incomplete win values can cause invalid or uninitialized accesses. Input read counts are unchecked.
programs.difficulty_reason: The windowed damped least-squares implementation requires multiple ordered tridiagonal solves and careful boundary handling.

test_cases.description: Smooth the full grid in both dimensions.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=32 ntr=8 | sustrip | smooth2 n1=32 n2=8 r1=4 r2=3 > out.bin

test_cases.description: Smooth a window with blurred edges and write relative errors.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=32 ntr=8 | sustrip | smooth2 n1=32 n2=8 r1=5 r2=2 win=4,28,1,7 rw=2 efile=error.bin > out.bin

programs.name: smooth3d
programs.purpose: Smooth a three-dimensional velocity grid with damped least squares, optionally smoothing slowness.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SMOOTH3D - 3D grid velocity SMOOTHing by the damped least squares

params.name: n1
params.description: Number of samples in the first dimension; must be positive.

params.name: n2
params.description: Number of samples in the second dimension; must be positive.

params.name: n3
params.description: Number of samples in the third dimension; must be positive.

params.name: r1
params.description: First-dimension operator length; forced to zero when n1<4 or d1<=0.

params.name: r2
params.description: Second-dimension operator length; forced to zero when n2<4 or d2<=0.

params.name: r3
params.description: Third-dimension operator length; forced to zero when n3<4 or d3<=0.

params.name: d1
params.description: First-dimension sample interval.

params.name: d2
params.description: Second-dimension sample interval.

params.name: d3
params.description: Third-dimension sample interval.

params.name: iter
params.description: Number of repeated smoothing solves; must be 1, 2, or 3.

params.name: time
params.description: Time-axis dimension; a nonzero value replaces depth.

params.name: depth
params.description: Depth-axis dimension used for weighting; overridden by a nonzero time.

params.name: mu
params.description: Relative smoothing weight at maximum depth or time; must be at least 1.

params.name: verbose
params.description: When nonzero, print minimum wavelengths to stderr.

params.name: slowness
params.description: When nonzero, invert velocity to slowness before smoothing and invert it back afterward.

params.name: vminc
params.description: Lower velocity clipping limit before smoothing.

params.name: vmaxc
params.description: Upper velocity clipping limit before smoothing.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Repeated float tridiagonal solves and sequential dimension passes are sensitive to arithmetic order and float/double mixing. Slowness conversion and verbose wavelength calculations divide by velocity, including zero; verbose also divides by sample intervals and uses sqrt. Multiple active dimensions overwrite allocated workspace pointers before freeing them, leaking earlier workspaces. Invalid depth or time values are not checked.
programs.difficulty_reason: The program performs repeated weighted tridiagonal solves across three dimensions with several coupled numerical options.

test_cases.description: Smooth all three dimensions with two iterations.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=16 ntr=16 | sustrip | smooth3d n1=16 n2=4 n3=4 d1=1 d2=2 d3=2 r1=4 r2=4 r3=4 iter=2 > out.bin

test_cases.description: Exercise clipping, slowness smoothing, time weighting, and wavelength reporting.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=16 ntr=16 | sustrip | smooth3d n1=16 n2=4 n3=4 r1=3 r2=2 r3=2 iter=3 time=2 mu=2 slowness=1 vminc=1 vmaxc=10 verbose=1 > out.bin

test_cases.description: Exercise a single iteration with second-dimension depth weighting.
test_cases.command: suplane nt=16 ntr=16 | sustrip | smooth3d n1=16 n2=4 n3=4 r1=2 r2=3 depth=2 mu=1.5 iter=1 > out.bin

programs.name: smoothint2
programs.purpose: Smooth nonuniformly sampled interfaces supplied as ASCII coordinate pairs.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: SMOOTHINT2 --- SMOOTH non-uniformly sampled INTerfaces, via the damped

params.name: ninf
params.description: Number of interfaces to read.

params.name: r
params.description: Smoothing parameter; the selfdoc incorrectly states a default of 100.

params.name: npmax
params.description: Maximum number of input entries per interface, including its terminating sentinel.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: smooth_1 performs two ordered float tridiagonal solves with float/double mixing and divides by squared coordinate spacing; duplicate adjacent x values cause an error. ASCII input and %g output introduce decimal conversion and output rounding. scanf return values are unchecked, so malformed or prematurely ended input can use uninitialized or stale values.
programs.difficulty_reason: The numerical core uses repeated tridiagonal solves on nonuniformly spaced coordinates.

test_cases.description: Smooth the five non-surface interfaces from the supplied demonstration model.
test_cases.command: unif2 tfile=in.txt && sed '1,3d' in.txt | smoothint2 ninf=5 npmax=101 r=100 > out.txt

test_cases.description: Exercise zero smoothing and a smaller interface count.
test_cases.command: unif2 tfile=in.txt && sed '1,3d' in.txt | smoothint2 ninf=2 npmax=20 r=0 > out.txt
